description: The shape scope of Content first: its answers, its usage rules and the semantic tokens it owns. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

answers.question: shape.count
answers.why: Control, badge and container corners differ.

answers.question: shape.definition
answers.why: One brand, one set of corners.

answers.question: shape.lands
answers.why: Corners show on buttons and article cards.

usage.why: Rounded corners match the warm reading tone. Sharp corners feel technical next to long text.
Pills sit softly next to text.
The option corner nests inside the menu corner. Soft, even curves keep the warm tone.
Text areas and list items share the control corner, so a form reads as one family.
Softer corners on cards and menus feel warm, like good paper.
A thin edge stays quiet beside long text. The words carry the page, not the lines.

usage.not: A ring that touches the control
usage.why: The ring stands clear of the control, so readers see focus on any fill.

badge.$description: Corner of badges, chips, tooltips, keyboard keys (kbd) and checkboxes: small labels and marks.

option.$description: Corner of options in menus and lists: the panel's corner less its padding, so the corners nest.

element.$description: Corner of an element that holds content and can grow past one line: a list item, an accordion row, a text area, a calendar, an attachment, a skeleton or media.

surface.$description: Corner of cards, menus and dialogs.

open-ds.why: We use a 1px default line for card and panel borders in order to give grouping where space alone does not, not separation: space separates groups here. A thin stroke does this by drawing a shared region with the least weight that still reads. So the lines stay quiet beside long text, because space separates groups (elevation.definition) and AA is the floor (accessibility.definition).

border-width.default.headline: One thin line.
border-width.default.line: Edges stay faint, so the reading leads.

radius.badge.headline: Round tags.
radius.badge.line: Badges and chips read as soft labels.

radius.control.headline: Soft controls.
radius.control.line: Buttons and inputs have a friendly, round corner.

radius.element.headline: Soft items.
radius.element.line: Rows, text areas and media share one round corner.

radius.option.headline: Corners that nest.
radius.option.line: An option's corner fits inside its menu's corner.

radius.surface.headline: Round cards.
radius.surface.line: Cards and dialogs feel calm and soft.
